judge_assessment.explanation: I re-derived all twelve problems and every keyed result is right. Vertex (4,1) with axis x = 4; |x+3|-5 shifts left 3 and down 5 with vertex (-3,-5); -2|x-1|+6 has vertex (1,6), opens down and is narrower; |x-2|-3 has vertex (2,-3) and x-intercepts -1 and 5; |x+1|-4 = 0 gives x = -5 and 3; -|x|+4 has vertex (0,4) and intercepts -4 and 4; 3|x+2|-7 has vertex (-2,-7), axis x = -2 and g(1) = 3(3)-7 = 2; 2|x-3|-8 = 0 gives -1 and 7 while 2|x-3|-8 = 4 gives -3 and 9; vertex (5,-2) through (7,4) forces 2a = 6 so a = 3; -2|x-4|+6 has y-intercept -2 and x-intercepts 1 and 7; vertex (-3,8) through (1,0) forces 4a = -8 so a = -2; and |2t-6|+1 = 2|t-3|+1 with vertex (3,1), reaching 5 at t = 1 and t = 5. The judge's 'all three graphical/manual responses have correct equations, landmarks, and usable grading guidance' is accurate and is this packet's real distinction - see the strengths. My one disagreement is with instruction_following at 4. Problem 12(b) reads 'Explain what the vertex means for the drone', and verify.json id 12 holds exactly three entries - an eval at t = 3, a solve for d(t) = 5, and an equiv proving |2t-6|+1 equals 2|t-3|+1 - with no manual entry. The author knew: final_response.md states in its own words that 'Problem 12(b), "explain what the vertex means for the drone", is likewise a written explanation - the key gives a model answer', and yet the verification file records problem 12 as three machine checks. The prompt says to clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review; the delivery prose labels it and the machine-readable artifact does not, which is the one place where a teacher grading from verify.json or from the Quick Answers row '12. 1, 1, 5, 2|t-3|+1' would not know to read anything. Two smaller slots are unbound the same way: problem 2 asks the student to 'Describe in words how the graph of g(x) = |x+3|-5 is obtained from f(x) = |x|', which is the primary requested output of that item and is verified only as the vertex numbers -3 and -5, and problem 3 asks whether the V opens up or down and whether it is narrower or wider than y = |x| - two categorical slots with no entries.

strengths_to_preserve: This is the batch's best handling of drawn responses and should be the template for the rest. Problems 4, 6 and 10 each carry a manual entry whose desc names the exact expected picture - 'Sketch of the V opening down from (0, 4) through (-4, 0) and (4, 0)' - sitting alongside verified eval and solve entries for the same id's vertex and intercepts. A hand grader gets the landmarks as checked numbers and the shape as a stated description, which is precisely what curr-277 (four sketches, zero manual entries) and curr-281 (ten sketches, one manual entry) are missing.

Problem 12 verifies the rewrite |2t - 6| + 1 = 2|t - 3| + 1 with an explicit equiv entry, so the factor-the-2-out-of-the-bars step - the one algebraic move on the sheet that a student is most likely to skip and that the vertex depends on - is a checked result rather than an assertion in the prose.

The ramp inverts direction cleanly at problem 9: items 1 to 8 go from equation to features, and items 9 and 11 go from features back to the equation, each verified with a genuine system entry over a and k rather than an eval of the answer. Problem 11 in particular gives only a vertex and one point, so a and k must both be recovered.

The two solve-from-graph problems (5 and 8) are framed as reading a picture the student is told about rather than one they must first draw, and problem 8 asks for the solutions of h(x) = 0 AND h(x) = 4 on the same V, which makes the horizontal-line idea explicit instead of implicit.

root_causes.description: Manual flagging is applied to whole problems whose entire product is a drawing, but not to the open half of an otherwise machine-checkable item. Problem 12 has three machine-verifiable parts and one explanation, so it was recorded as three entries; because the contract only requires at least one check per id, nothing detects that a printed response slot is unrepresented. The delivery prose noticed the gap and the artifact did not, which shows the classification happened during write-up rather than during verification planning.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 12(b): 'Explain what the vertex means for the drone.' verify.json id 12 holds an eval (Abs(2*t-6)+1 at t=3 = 1), a solve (expected [1,5]) and an equiv - no manual entry.

final_response.md: 'Problem 12(b), "explain what the vertex means for the drone", is likewise a written explanation - the key gives a model answer.' The same paragraph says 'The three items flagged for manual review are exactly the three that cannot be machine-checked: the sketches themselves on problems 4, 6 and 10', so 12(b) was consciously excluded.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers row 12 reads '1, 1, 5, 2|t - 3| + 1' with no manual marker.
worksheet.pdf problem 2 asks for a verbal description of the transformation; verify.json id 2 holds a solve expecting -3 and an eval expecting -5 - the vertex, not the description.

worksheet.pdf problem 3 asks 'say whether the V opens up or down, and say whether the graph is narrower or wider than y = |x|'; verify.json id 3 holds a solve expecting 1 and an eval expecting 6, with no representation for either categorical answer.

improvements.title: Flag problem 12(b) and problem 2's verbal description, applying the gate per slot rather than per problem
improvements.proposed_change: Run the open-response gate over each printed response slot, so an id that already carries machine entries still fails when one of its slots is an explanation or a verbal description. Add a manual entry under id 12 whose desc states what the reader should find (the vertex (3,1) is the moment the drone is nearest the trailhead, 1 km away, at t = 3 minutes, and the distance rises symmetrically on either side) and one under id 2 for the requested description (shift left 3, down 5). Cross-check the gate against final_response.md: when the delivery prose names an item as a written explanation and verify.json has no manual entry for that id, that alone should be a build failure, since the two artifacts are then in contradiction.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: curr-297's problem 12 prose with its three existing machine entries and no manual entry. The slot-level gate must exit non-zero naming 12(b). Adding a manual entry under id 12 must make it pass and must make the rendered bank row carry the manual marker. Add a second assertion that a final_response.md naming an item as a written explanation while verify.json has no manual entry for that id also fails.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the last gap in what is otherwise the batch's best-flagged packet, and the final_response cross-check would catch this class automatically wherever the author already noticed the item is open - which, judging by this case, is often.
improvements.risk: The final_response cross-check depends on prose phrasing and will misfire when the delivery text discusses an item's explanation in the answer key rather than on the worksheet; it should be advisory before it is promoted to a hard gate.

improvements.title: Represent categorical feature answers (opens up or down, narrower or wider) as checked results
improvements.proposed_change: Add a categorical check to scripts/verify.py that derives opening direction from the sign of a and relative width from the absolute value of a compared with 1, so problem 3's 'opens down' and 'narrower' become verified expecteds rather than prose. Extend the slot inventory to require one binding per requested feature, which also covers problem 1's axis equation and problem 7's axis equation - both currently implied by a solve of the inside-the-bars expression rather than declared as the answer 'x = 4' and 'x = -2'.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: curr-297's problem 3 prose ('give the vertex, say whether the V opens up or down, and say whether the graph is narrower or wider than y = |x|') with the two existing numeric entries. The slot gate must exit non-zero naming the two categorical slots. Adding categorical entries derived from a = -2 must make it pass and must make the bank row read with 'opens down' and 'narrower' rather than the bare '1, 6'.
improvements.expected_impact: Puts the transformation vocabulary the sheet teaches under the same verification as its numbers, and makes the fast-grading bank usable for the description-style items instead of showing only their vertex coordinates.
improvements.risk: Categorical checks are only as good as the coefficient extraction behind them; for a function the parser cannot put in a|x-h|+k form the check must degrade to manual rather than guess.

case_summary: Complete and mathematically correct absolute-value transformation practice - I re-derived all twelve items independently (vertices, axes, intercepts, the two feature-to-equation recoveries a = 3, k = -2 and a = -2, k = 8, and the drone times t = 1 and t = 5) with no discrepancy. This packet is also the batch's benchmark for drawn responses: problems 4, 6 and 10 each pair verified landmark values with a manual entry whose desc states the exact picture expected, which is what the other graphing-heavy cases in this batch (curr-277 with four unflagged sketches, curr-281 with nine) should copy. The one real gap is problem 12(b), 'Explain what the vertex means for the drone', which verify.json records as part of a three-entry machine-checked id even though final_response.md itself describes it as a written explanation - the delivery prose and the machine-readable artifact contradict each other, and only the prose is right. Problem 2's requested verbal description and problem 3's two categorical judgements are unbound in the same way. None of this disturbs the ACCEPT.
